chunks: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him)

That Al-Qa'im will descend from the defile of Thi Tuwa with the number of the people of Badr - three hundred and thirteen men - until he leans his back against the Black Stone, and shakes the victorious banner. Ali ibn Abu Hamza said: I mentioned that to Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far, and he said: It is an evidenced book.

key_terms.أَهْلُ بَدْرٍ: Ahl al-Badr (The People of Badr), referring to the 313 companions of the Prophet
key_terms.الْحَجَرُ الْأَسْوَدُ: Al-Hajar al-Aswad (The Black Stone), located in the Kaaba
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: Al-Qa'im (The Riser), a title for the Twelfth Imam
key_terms.ثَنِيَّةُ ذِي طَوًى: Thaniyyat Thi Tuwa (The Defile of Thi Tuwa), a location in Mecca
key_terms.كِتَابٌ مَنْشُورٌ: Kitab Manshur (An Evidenced/Opened Book), indicating authenticity from a written source

ai.seo_question: Who is Al-Qa'im and what are the signs of his descent according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the eschatological significance of the number 313, linking the Mahdi’s emergence directly to the archetypal victory at Badr. The specific detail of leaning against the Black Stone (*Hajar al-Aswad*) underscores the sanctity of the Kaaba as the spiritual and political center of his authority. Imam Musa al-Kadim’s affirmation that this is from a 'written source' (*kitab munshur*) validates its status as a well-established tradition within Shia scholarly circles.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (9) Ali bin al-Husayn narrated from Muhammad bin Yahya from Muhammad bin Hassaan ar-Razi from Muhammad bin Ali al-Kufi from Ali bin al-Hakam from Ali bin Abu Hamza from Abu Baseer that

Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) had said: “Al-Qa’im will come from the defile of Mountain Thi Tuwa with three hundred and thirteen men as the number of the Muslims, who have fought in the battle of Badr. He will lean his back against the Black Rock (in the Kaaba) and will shake his victorious banner.” Ali bin Abu Hamza said: “I mentioned that to Abul Hasan Musa bin Ja’far al-Kadhim (as) and he said: “It is an evidenced book.”
